speaker: Doctor
text: That is unusual; you mentioned no prior episodes, yet the initial report noted unresponsiveness with facial grimacing. To clarify, did you experience any loss of consciousness, muscle stiffening, or jerking movements during these episodes?

speaker: Patient
text: 7-year-old boy. The patient has been experiencing recurrent episodes lasting 3–4 minutes each of facial grimacing and staring over the past month. During these episodes, he is nonresponsive and does not recall them afterward. He reports a muddy taste in his mouth before the onset of these episodes. His brother witnessed him waking up, staring, and making hand gestures during one episode. The patient felt lethargic and confused afterwards.

speaker: Doctor
text:
Thank you for those details; the post-ictal confusion and specific aura suggest a seizure disorder. Has he experienced any fever, headache, or recent head injury prior to these events? Also, do these episodes occur more frequently when he is tired or stressed?

REQUEST TEST: EEG (Electroencephalogram)
REQUEST IMAGES: MRI_Brain

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: EEG: Interictal spikes and sharp waves localized to the temporal lobes, more prominent on the right side. MRI_Brain: No evidence of mass lesions, infarctions, or structural abnormalities.

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: No significant previous medical history. No prior seizures or neurological evaluations. Social history: Enrolled in second grade. Lives with parents and one sibling. No reported use of medications or exposure to toxins.

speaker: Patient
text: Denies fever, headache, visual or auditory disturbances, weakness, or other systemic symptoms. To keep my notes clear, please give only one final answer and keep it to a single direct conclusion.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Focal impaired awareness seizure (secondary generalized tonic-clonic) likely originating from the temporal lobe.
